To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have improved the orbital parameters of a transiting planet and have confirmed the transit ephemeris.
we observed 7 transits and 31 nights of observations in 2007, that we improved the orbital parameters of TrES-2, that we could detect a transit in our first light curve of this star.
we could detect the transit of TrES-2b and determine the orbital parameters of TrES- 2b with higher precision than before.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the photometric monitoring of transiting extrasolar planets and the improvement of the orbital parameters.
the detection of transits of extrasolar planets, and the determination of the orbital and physical parameters of the planets.
the photometric monitoring of stars with known transits.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we could confirm the planetary transits of TrES-2, and that the transit depth is 0.014 mag, the orbital period 2.47124d and the time of the transit mid-point is HJD = 244 6009.4.
the TrES- 2 system is well suited for follow-up observations with the AIU telescope.
the TrES- 2 system is very stable and well suited for follow-up observations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our results are in good agreement with the results published by Winn et al. (2006), but we could improve the ephemeris and the orbital inclination.
we have shown, that our setup and methods are suitable for high precision photometric observations.
we could show that it is possible to observe the transits of the transiting planets with a small telescope and a CCD-camera.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have shown that it is possible to observe transits of planets around stars with a magnitude of 11.7 from a small telescope with a CCD camera.
our AIU Jena system can detect transits of TrES-2 and that the AIU Jema system is a good tool for follow-up observations of transiting planets.
the photometric precision obtained by the AIU JENA telescope is sufficient for the detection of planetary transits and for the determination of the orbital parameters.
